title: Systematic review of indoor soundscape assessments: Activity-based psycho-acoustics analysis
review_question: This study aimed to investigate how psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics could be applied in indoor soundscape studies by conducting a systematic review of peer-reviewed publications spanning the past 15 years. We considered the following research questions: (i) what psycho-acoustic indicators can be utilized to obtain an objective soundscape assessment? and (ii) do soundscape descriptors vary with the desired activities within the indoor space?
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Peer-reviewed journal papers published over the last 20 years, matching keywords 'psycho-acoustic', 'indoor', and 'soundscape'. Papers must include psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics and perceived annoyance factors, incorporate soundscape concepts focusing on human sound perceptions, and be restricted to indoor spaces. Excluded: review papers, books, book chapters, urban soundscape studies, or studies lacking psycho-acoustical analysis.

synthesis_conclusions: Psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics (loudness, sharpness, fluctuation strength, roughness, tonality) are frequently utilized to assess sound perception in indoor soundscape studies.
Soundscape descriptors and response variables exhibit distinct variations depending on the specific utilization and desired activities within each indoor space.
Models for affective response in indoor spaces should be developed considering the specific activities and usage of the targeted area.
Very few papers have addressed work-related quality aspects (productivity, job satisfaction, willingness to work, work efficiency) using psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics.
evidence_gaps: Lack of sufficient research on prediction models based on psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics within indoor soundscapes.
Insufficient studies integrating psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics into work-related quality aspects (productivity, job satisfaction, willingness to work, work efficiency).
Need to develop soundscape dimensions appropriate for indoor settings, as existing ISO standards (e.g., ISO TS 12913-3) were developed for outdoor environments.
A complete model for assessing affective response to soundscapes in school buildings has not yet been provided.
limitations: The review did not consider non-peer-reviewed articles.
The study is a first step in an emerging scientific field, suggesting a need for more comprehensive research.

paper_metadata.crossref_title: Systematic review of indoor soundscape assessments: Activity-based psycho-acoustics analysis
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: This study examines 22 peer-reviewed papers to offer insights into the current utilization of psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics in research focused on indoor soundscapes. The selection of papers followed the PRISMA method for systematic review, followed by descriptive and bibliometric analyses. The review focuses on (i) identifying what psycho-acoustic indicators can be utilized to obtain an objective soundscape assessment, and (ii) determining if soundscape descriptors vary with the desired activities within the indoor space. The findings provide an overview of how psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics are used to predict perceived annoyance in indoor environments. The discussion delves into response variables related to occupants’ sound perception across various indoor settings. It highlights the lack of sufficient research on prediction models based on psycho-acoustic sound quality metrics within indoor soundscapes. Further research is required to develop tools enabling the optimal design of indoor soundscapes, which can vary according to the intended use of the room.
